title: The week's low, and a shift
prompt: It is 10:02 ET. Read the chart and decide.

intro.beginner: A downtrend has reached the lowest point of the week, and price has just moved sharply the other way. Think about what's confirmed and what isn't.

whyNot.label: shorting the displacement
whyNot.why: The Daily and 4H are still down, so a short is with the trend, and it's also selling right after the week's low was swept and a violent displacement printed through structure. It's a coin flip: with the trend, against the evidence on the lower timeframe.

whyNot.label: buying with full size
whyNot.why: The higher timeframe hasn't shifted: this is a lower-timeframe reversal inside a larger downtrend. A long is valid with a plan that respects that, a nearer target and a stop beyond the sweep.

reference.summary: The week's low is swept and price displaces up violently through the last 5m high. Whether this is a reversal or a retrace in a Daily and 4H downtrend is open: a long to the previous day high (or its midpoint) is valid, waiting for a 1H or 4H shift is equally valid, and standing aside is defensible. Several readings hold up; none is certain.

bias.why: The Daily and 4H are still in a downtrend, and the week's low just got swept: neutral, or a bullish read with the shift still unconfirmed, are both defensible. Staying bearish isn't unreasonable either.

decision.why: A long from the gap with a defined target is valid. So is waiting for the higher timeframe to confirm. Standing aside is defensible given the counter-trend risk.

take.why: Valid as a counter-trend long with a plan; a pass is equally reasonable.

draw.why: If it's a reversal, the previous day high is the pool; if it's a retrace, the week's low is still the draw.

location.why: Price is near the bottom of the week's range.

next_objective.why: Price was drawn to the previous day high (21,993.25); it also traded to the day's high (21,951.75) and the unfilled gap at 21,871 to 21,878.25 on the way, which makes those defensible too. The question is where price was likely to be pulled, not what the next candle would do. A previous-day extreme is also a pool of buy-side or sell-side liquidity, so that answer is right on the side, if less exact.

annotations.label: Week low 21,785.25
annotations.why: The week's obvious sell-side liquidity: taken at 09:34, the reason this is a reversal candidate at all.

annotations.label: Previous day high 21,993.25
annotations.why: The draw if this is a reversal.

annotations.label: Midpoint of yesterday's range 21,889.25
annotations.why: A nearer draw (equilibrium) that fits a cautious counter-trend plan.

annotations.label: 5m bullish FVG from the displacement
annotations.why: The entry model if you take the long.

confluences.label: The week's low swept
confluences.why: The biggest pool in sight, taken.

confluences.label: A violent displacement through the last 5m high
confluences.why: The shift on the lower timeframe.

confluences.label: Daily and 4H still trending down
confluences.why: Not a reason to go long. A reason to size it as counter-trend or wait.

trade.confirmationLabel: the displacement that closed above the last 5m high

lookFor: Some charts have no single right answer. A reversal and a retrace both fit; the skill is a plan that survives either.
Say what would convince you it's a reversal (a 1H break of structure) before it happens.
A counter-trend long needs a nearer target or a smaller idea. A trend long doesn't.
